entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

tourism.detail: Australians may visit for tourism for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, subject to border evidence and the shared Schengen count.
tourism.next: Carry proof of accommodation, funds and return or onward travel and recalculate the rolling total.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.detail: Spain's entry guidance recognises company or authority invitations, evidence of a professional relationship and trade-fair or congress access cards as proof of a short business purpose.
meetings.next: Keep the trip to meetings, negotiation, investigation and relationship building rather than contracted delivery.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.detail: Conference attendance can use the short business front door with registration or an access card. Speaking, training, performing and paid event duties are separate.
conference.next: Carry registration and invitation and reclassify the trip immediately if the organiser adds a programmed role.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.route: Visitor only if the exact non-gainful activity is accepted; otherwise a work, exemption or cultural route
unpaid-speaking.detail: Spain publishes a visitor lane for non-gainful activity and named exemptions for university, public-research and artist work, but no broad official rule making every unpaid conference talk a visitor activity.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the organiser and competent Spanish consulate confirm the exact zero-fee role, expenses, commercial context and visa requirement before departure.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: Self-employed or employee work visa; named work-permit exemption where the facts qualify
paid-speaking.detail: The Sydney Consulate says remunerated activity requires a visa whatever its duration. Professors invited by Spanish universities, certain public researchers and artists can use specific exemption-visa processes; a general keynote does not automatically fit.
paid-speaking.next: Give the host and consulate the contract, payment, duration and professional category and secure the visa before travel.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Visa-free publisher and rights meetings plus separately classified public appearance
book-launch.detail: Business discussions can use the visitor lane, while a remunerated reading or professional launch requires a visa and a zero-fee programmed appearance still needs classification. Direct retail and imported stock add commercial and customs layers.
book-launch.next: Use a Spanish publisher or bookseller for local stock and receipts and classify the author appearance separately.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: University work-permit-exemption visa where invited; self-employed or employee route otherwise
ai-teaching.detail: Professors, technicians, researchers and scientists invited or hired by a Spanish university for teaching, research or academic tasks are named in the exemption system, with different visa treatment by length. Corporate training or a continuing teaching role needs its applicable work route.
ai-teaching.next: Have the university's legal representative issue the invitation or contract; otherwise use the normal self-employed or employee process.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.route: International Telework or Digital Nomad visa
remote-work.detail: The route supports remote work for an employer or company outside Spain using telecommunications. A self-employed applicant may have Spanish work up to 20% of total professional activity and must show a degree or at least three years' current-field experience, a prior relationship with the foreign company and social-security compliance.
remote-work.next: Use the Australian consular checklist and obtain employer or client consent, company evidence, qualification evidence and the correct social-security certificate or Spanish registration.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: Entrepreneur visa or residence authorisation under Law 14/2013
entrepreneur.detail: The project must be innovative or of special economic interest for Spain and receive a favourable report. Current UGE guidance says there is no fixed minimum investment or job-creation number; it evaluates the founder, plan, finance, innovation and added value.
entrepreneur.next: Prepare the founder profile, business plan and financing and seek the favourable project report before moving to operate.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Visa-free meetings, fairs and negotiations; work and commercial permission for service delivery
trade.detail: Professional visits and trade-fair access are recognised short-stay evidence. Selling directly, installing, training customers or fulfilling a contract locally can become remunerated work.
trade.next: Use the first trip for partners and contracts, then map importer, seller, service delivery, tax and work status.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Artist work-permit-exemption visa or audiovisual and cultural-sector route
artist.detail: Artists performing in Spain appear in the exemption-visa system, and the UGE manages residence pathways for audiovisual and cultural workers. The correct process depends on duration, production, contract and role.
artist.next: Have the Spanish promoter identify the artist or cultural process, list all dates and payments and obtain the visa or authorisation before performance.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Visa-free visitor elements plus a visa or authorisation for every active or remunerated element
mixed-mission.detail: Tourism, meetings and attendance can share the short stay. A talk, course, consulting session, performance, remote-work base or direct sale retains its own boundary.
mixed-mission.next: Build one dated schedule and obtain written host or consular classification for each active item before travel.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Spain, Yarralumla about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Spain, Yarralumla if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering programmes over 90 days need a national long-stay visa, an agreement with a legally registered organisation, funds, insurance and a medical certificate (police check over 6 months). Apply 2 months ahead. Short visits are not addressed.
volunteering.next: Ask the consulate about stays under 90 days.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency of Spain is the Euro (€). If you're travelling to or from any non-European Union (EU) country, declare funds of 10,000 Euro or more, including the equivalent in another currency. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you fail to declare currency or give wrong information, you'll be fined. You don't need to declare funds if you're travelling to or from another EU country.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Spain is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Get a legible entry stamp at the first Schengen entry; airlines may check you haven't overstayed 90 days.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: A Spanish university, organiser, promoter or customer can provide the invitation or contract and identify whether the activity uses a work-permit-exemption visa, self-employed work visa, employee route, entrepreneur route or cultural-sector process.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Carry proof of purpose and split every active appearance from attendance. If there is any fee, honorarium or other remuneration, obtain the correct Spanish visa before travel.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: The short-stay ceiling is 90 days in 180 across Schengen. International telework, entrepreneur and work routes support residence when Spain becomes a base or place of delivery.
baseline_unverified.from: Luke's earlier precursor notes; not verified against an official source and not an authority. Kept because no official page covers this point yet.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

AESA (the Spanish aviation safety agency) registers UAS operators through its online UAS application. Operators from outside the EASA states register in the first EASA state where they plan to operate; if that is Spain, the Spanish procedure applies. An operator can be registered in only one member state at a time.
Operators registered in another EU state who need Specific-category operations in Spain file a cross-border request with AESA (guide Ed.02; check the current edition).

Spain's UAS geographical zones are published through ENAIRE Drones (drones.enaire.es) and the AIP, under Royal Decree 517/2024. AESA says the flight rules and zones apply equally to recreational and professional flights, and that some zones (for example military areas) are not managed by ENAIRE and need coordination or prior authorisation from the zone holder.
